## 2026-09-24 — GEO-32 (PA-SC and PA-5 are incomparable)

Kind: claim. Claim it bears on: GEO-32, `claims/GEO-32.md`, "Neither of PA-SC and PA-5 implies
the other, even under PA-4", created 2026-09-24 with Roey's redefinition of PA-5.
Commit audited: n/a (claim verification)

Model note: both runs on `claude-opus-5-5`, an equal primary with Fable 5.1 (Roey, 2026-09-24).
An earlier run-A dispatch on Fable 5.1 failed at the API usage limit before returning, and
counts for nothing. The runs were sequential: B was dispatched after A returned Proved, on an
identical brief.

Run A, verbatim:

```
VERDICT
item:       GEO-32 (no old alias; created 2026-09-24)
label:      Proved
confidence: CONFIRMED
model:      claude-opus-5-5 (Opus 5.5 — an equal primary for clearing per Roey 2026-09-24)
inputs:     none
blocking:   none for the statement; but the label rests on this report's construction and checks, not on the file's sketch — as written its Proof establishes only direction (b) at garage level; F1 and F2 must be written into the Proof when the label is applied
```

Run B, verbatim:

```
VERDICT
item:       GEO-32 (no old alias; new 2026-09-24)
label:      Proved
confidence: CONFIRMED
model:      claude-opus-5-5 (Opus 5.5, equal primary — full strength)
inputs:     none
blocking:   none for the label; two conditions on transcription — write in the explicit PA-SC-not-PA-5 witness (finding 1), which the file leaves as "the check to make"; and say whether the conditions are on the garage P or on the origami M (finding 2)
```

GEO-32 findings, both runs:
- **Missing witness for PA-SC ⇏ PA-5 (both runs, UNJUSTIFIED → ADD_DERIVATION).** Gauss–Bonnet
  is only a necessary condition. The witness both runs found independently is the
  **8-square fan**: squares $Q_1,\dots,Q_8$ around one vertex $v$, with $Q_j$ in quadrant
  $j \bmod 4$ and consecutive squares glued along their edge from $v$, except $Q_8|Q_1$. Run A
  describes it as the two-sheeted $[-1,1]^2$ branched at 0 and cut along $[0,1]\times\{0\}$. It
  has $\chi=1$, ten corners of angle $\pi/2$, one of $4\pi$ ($m=8$), seven boundary points of
  angle $\pi$, and no interior cone points; Gauss–Bonnet gives $10\cdot\pi/2-3\pi=2\pi$. Its
  unfolding has 32 squares, genus 4, $\mathcal H(3,3)$. A smaller witness: the $2\times2$ square
  slit from its centre to a side midpoint, with one $2\pi$ corner, $\chi=1$, unfolding in
  $\mathcal H(1,1)$. Angles $\ge2\pi$ are allowed at PA-4: CW12 `parking.tex` l. 503–505, "no
  apriori upper bound on the angle at a vertex" (run A).
- **PA-5 ⇏ PA-SC (both runs).** The $3\times3$ square frame (embedded, not simple) has corners
  $\{\pi/2{:}4,\ 3\pi/2{:}4\}$ and $\chi=0$.
- **Garage or origami (both runs, ambiguity → state the reading).** Both runs prove the
  garage-level reading. For the origami-level reading ("M is the unfolding of some P with …"):
  - (a) no garage structure on the fan's $M$ is PA-5, because $[\sigma,\tau]$ has two 4-cycles
    and by GEO-9 (Proved) a PA-5 garage produces only odd cycles. This is by hand, in both runs.
  - (b) no garage structure on the frame's $M$ is simply connected. Both runs enumerate the
    free $K_4$-structures (run A: 16 commuting pairs, one garage; run B: 9 structures, one
    garage). Both also give a hyperellipticity route: a simply connected $P$ forces $\mu\nu$ to
    have $2g+2=12$ fixed points, but the derivative-$(-I)$ involutions have 8, 0, 8 and 8.
    Run A derived these counts by hand from the frame's symmetries (only $|C|=4$ came from the
    script). Run B notes that under the repo's rule its computational route alone would give at
    most "modulo".
- **Understated (run B).** The 6-square fan has a $3\pi$ corner and satisfies PA-4, PA-SC and
  PA-5w but not PA-5. So PA-SC does not imply PA-5 even under PA-5w. The same examples also
  show PA-SC and PA-5w incomparable (run A F4), which until now rested on R §0.2 alone, with
  the same Gauss–Bonnet gap.
- **Drift.** "square-frame polyomino" in the summary clashes with PA-6's "polyomino" = simple;
  write "the $3\times3$ square frame (embedded, not simple)". `assumptions/PA-5.md`'s summary
  still says "turning point". `CLAUDE.md` still says "PA-6 ⇒ PA-5 is pending (GEO-31)".
- **Leads, not findings (route separately).**
  - OPEN-10: for any PA-4 garage, the fixed points of $\mu\nu$ are exactly the lifts of the odd
    corners, and $\chi(M)=4\chi(P)-\#\mathrm{odd}$. So $\mu\nu$ has $2g+2$ fixed points iff
    $\chi(P)=1$; equivalently $M/\langle\mu\nu\rangle$ is the double of $P$. That would answer
    OPEN-10 affirmatively for $\iota=\mu\nu$. Both runs observed this; neither verified it as
    an item.
  - GEO-19 (N3), run A: its test is not sufficient. On the frame's $M$, two $K_4$-structures
    pass it, but their quotient has interior holonomy $-I$, so it is not a garage; two more
    flip 8 edges under $\mu\nu$.
- Scripts: scratchpad `geo32_check.py`…`geo32_check4.py` (A), `geo32_ref.py`, `geo32_ref2.py` (B),
  on named examples only.

Decision: **Proved / Proved → GEO-32, Proved** in the garage-level reading, with the witnesses
written in.
Allowed wording: "(Garage level.) There is a PA-4 garage that is simply connected and not PA-5,
and one that is PA-5 and not simply connected; so neither of PA-SC and PA-5 implies the other,
even under PA-4. Witnesses: the 8-square fan (one $4\pi$ corner, ten $\pi/2$ corners,
$\chi=1$; or the slit $2\times2$ square with one $2\pi$ corner) and the $3\times3$ square frame
(embedded, not simple; corners $\pi/2$ and $3\pi/2$ only, $\chi=0$). The same examples show
PA-SC and PA-5w incomparable. (Origami level, half (a): no garage structure on the fan's
unfolding is PA-5, since $[\sigma,\tau]$ has 4-cycles (GEO-9).)" The origami-level half (b),
for the frame's unfolding, goes in Notes with both routes and the remark that the hand route
is run A's. It is not part of the label.
Open: the OPEN-10 lead ($\mu\nu$ hyperelliptic iff $\chi(P)=1$) as a new item; GEO-19's
insufficiency, as a note on GEO-19; the origami-level half (b) as an item, if wanted.

## 2026-09-24 — OPEN-10 (under PA-SC, the OA-2 involution is hyperelliptic): attestation

Kind: attestation, by Roey. This is not a `claim-verifier` pass. It is recorded so that the
label's provenance stays visible.

Roey, verbatim (2026-09-24): "OPEN-10 does hold, I vouch for it."

The argument on record is the lead both `claim-verifier` runs on GEO-32 observed
(`computation/verdicts/2026-09-24_GEO-32.md`). Neither run verified it as an item:

> For any PA-4 garage, the fixed points of $\mu\nu$ are exactly the lifts of the odd corners,
> and $\chi(M)=4\chi(P)-\#\mathrm{odd}$. So $\mu\nu$ has $2g+2$ fixed points iff $\chi(P)=1$;
> equivalently $M/\langle\mu\nu\rangle$ is the double of $P$.

Under PA-SC, $P$ is a disc, so $\chi(P)=1$ and $\mu\nu$ is hyperelliptic.

Decision: **attested → OPEN-10, Proved**, for $\iota=\mu\nu=\phi(-1,-1)$, the involution the
garage provides. Scope: the item asks about "the involution of (A2)". This attestation
covers $\iota=\mu\nu$. Whether *every* OA-2 involution of $M$ is hyperelliptic under PA-SC is
not covered.
Allowed wording: "Under PA-SC (with PA-4), the involution $\mu\nu$ is hyperelliptic:
$M/\langle\mu\nu\rangle$ is the double of $P$, a sphere, and $\mu\nu$ has $2g+2$ fixed points.
More generally, for a PA-4 garage, $\mu\nu$ is hyperelliptic iff $\chi(P)=1$. (Attested by
Roey, 2026-09-24; not machine-verified.)"
Open: a `/verify-claim` pass, if a machine check is ever wanted; and the general-$\iota$ question.
